name: DRAGIN - Dynamic Retrieval Augmented Generation based on the real-time Information Needs of Large Language Models
venue: ACL 2024 (Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Main Conference, Long Paper, Oral; pages 12991-13013). Preprint arXiv:2403.10081 (v1 Mar 2024, v3 Sep 2024).
authors_affiliation: Weihang Su, Yichen Tang (equal contribution), Qingyao Ai (corresponding author), Yiqun Liu - Department of Computer Science and Technology, Tsinghua University; Zhijing Wu - School of Computer Science and Technology, Beijing Institute of Technology.
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/oneal2000/DRAGIN (actively maintained; rebranded 'DRAGIN & Dynamic RAG Toolbox' with updated reproducibility guide and bug fixes through 2025).
task_domain: QA / knowledge-intensive text generation - multi-hop QA (2WikiMultihopQA, HotpotQA), reading comprehension (IIRC), and commonsense reasoning (StrategyQA), all framed as knowledge-intensive multi-step generation with chain-of-thought.
problem_setting: Single-agent, offline non-interactive inference with a frozen, training-free LLM (no fine-tuning, no prompt engineering, no additional parameters). DRAGIN is a dynamic/active RAG framework that, during the LLM's left-to-right autoregressive generation of a CoT-style answer, decides in real time WHEN to pause generation and trigger retrieval and WHAT query to issue, then injects retrieved passages and continues generation. It can be plugged into any open-source Transformer-based LLM whose token-probability distribution and self-attention scores are accessible (a stated limitation is that closed APIs without attention access are not supported). Supervision is limited to few-shot CoT in-context exemplars (fewshot = 6); the only tunable knobs are the RIND threshold theta and top-k token-keep budget. Greedy decoding is used for reproducibility.
what_is_retrieved: Documents/passages (100-token Wikipedia passages) from a static external corpus.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: Wikipedia (DPR psgs_w100 dump, ~21M 100-token passages) indexed once offline in Elasticsearch (BM25) or encoded by SGPT. No agent-written growing/episodic memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking: each retrieval call returns a fixed retrieve_topk = 3 passages (the three most relevant passages replace the previous retrieved set). There is no notion of recovering a complete minimal set or precision-driven variable-size selection; only the number of retrieval EVENTS varies (driven by RIND triggers), not k per event.
retrieval_unit: document (100-token Wikipedia passage). The retrieval QUERY is built at token granularity (a bag of self-attention-selected content tokens), but the retrieved unit is a passage/document.
index_source: Static corpus, constructed offline (Wikipedia DPR dump indexed once in Elasticsearch/BM25, or SGPT-encoded). Not test-time-induced and does not grow online.
index_structure_topology: Flat index: BM25 inverted index in Elasticsearch (main setting), or a flat dense-vector store of SGPT passage embeddings (alternative). No graph, hierarchy, or cluster structure.
retriever_type: Off-the-shelf retriever, retriever-agnostic by design: BM25 (sparse lexical, default, Elasticsearch) is the main retriever; a SOTA dense retriever SGPT (Muennighoff 2022) is tested as an alternative. BM25 consistently outperforms SGPT inside DRAGIN.
retriever_learning_signal: None - the retriever (BM25 or SGPT) is entirely off-the-shelf and is not trained, fine-tuned, or selected via any learning signal (no contrastive, LM-feedback, preference, RL, or value-based training). DRAGIN's contribution is in WHEN and WHAT to query, not in learning the retriever; the LLM's self-attention determines the query content without any retriever-side training.
query_construction: QFS (Query Formulation based on Self-attention): when RIND triggers retrieval at token position i, QFS extracts the self-attention scores of the LAST Transformer layer that token t_i assigned to all preceding tokens {t_1..t_{i-1}}, sorts them descending, selects the top-n highest-attention tokens, maps them back to words, re-orders the words by their original position in the text, and concatenates them into the retrieval query. This pulls the query from the LLM's information needs across the ENTIRE generated context rather than just the last sentence/last few tokens. (Code option `query_formulation: real_words`; `retrieve_keep_top_k` ~35-40 tokens.)
query_granularity: Step/token-level (trigger-position-level): a fresh query is formulated dynamically at each retrieval-trigger token position during generation, conditioned on the entire preceding context via self-attention. Not a single task-level query at t=0.
when_to_retrieve: Active (uncertainty-triggered) and iterative: retrieval is triggered dynamically during generation whenever the real-time information-need signal exceeds a threshold, and this can fire multiple times within one answer (multi-round). Distinct from one-shot retrieval and from fixed-schedule iterative retrieval.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Attention + uncertainty + semantics combined (RIND - Real-time Information Needs Detection). For each generated token t_i a score S_RIND(t_i) = H_i * a_max(i) * s_i is computed, where H_i is the entropy of the token's output probability distribution over the vocabulary (uncertainty), a_max(i) is the maximum self-attention this token receives from all FOLLOWING tokens in the last Transformer layer (its influence on subsequent generation), and s_i is a binary semantic indicator that is 0 for stopwords (filtered via spaCy en_core_web_sm) and 1 otherwise. Retrieval activates when any token's S_RIND exceeds a predefined threshold theta (default ~0.6-1.2 depending on config). This is a richer signal than FLARE's pure next-token-probability rule.
reranking: None - no reranking stage; the retriever returns the top-3 passages directly for the QFS-formulated query.
retrieved_context_refinement: None - retrieved passages are used verbatim; no rerank, decompose-recompose, distillation, distractor filtering, or compression. At a new trigger position j the newly retrieved 3 passages simply REPLACE the previously injected ones (the generation is also truncated back to the trigger position before re-generating with new evidence).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the 3 retrieved passages are inserted via a fixed prompt template ('Below are the external knowledge references: [1].. [2].. [3].. Please answer the question based on the external knowledge: Question: ... Answer: T'') and the LLM continues generation from the truncated output T' (the prefix up to the trigger token). No training signal or latent injection.
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved retrieve-during-generation inside a single autoregressive decoding loop: generate -> RIND detects an information need at a token -> truncate output at that token -> QFS forms a query -> retrieve top-3 -> prepend evidence -> resume generation, repeating whenever RIND fires. It is reasoning/generation-guided iterative retrieval, not tree search, MCTS, or hierarchical subtask planning.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-sentence-or-token: retrieval is woven in at the token position where RIND's real-time-information-need score crosses the threshold, which is finer-grained than FLARE's per-sentence rule and the fixed per-n-token / per-sentence baselines.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw retrieved passages (verbatim 100-token Wikipedia text) injected into the prompt; not distilled, summarized, or converted to structured notes.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw document/passage (no abstraction or distillation of the retrieved unit).
noise_robustness_mechanism: Largely none/implicit: DRAGIN adds no retriever-aware training, relevance evaluator, self-reflection, or distractor-aware SFT. Robustness comes only from (a) RIND firing retrieval only when truly needed (avoiding low-value retrieval that the paper shows can hurt, e.g., FL-RAG/FS-RAG sometimes below single-round), and (b) QFS issuing more targeted queries. The paper's case study explicitly notes a failure mode: weaker long-context LLMs (e.g., LLaMA-7B) can get confused by multiple injected passages, so noise robustness is acknowledged as a limitation, not solved.
memory_type: none - no episodic, skill, workflow, procedural, graph, or latent memory; only a transient per-question generation buffer (the in-progress output and the currently injected passages, which are replaced on each new trigger and reset per question).
write_back: false - DRAGIN does not store any new experiences, cases, or skills; nothing is written to a persistent store across questions.
online_growth: false - the retrievable store (Wikipedia BM25/SGPT index) is fixed/frozen after offline construction and does not grow during deployment.
write_back_trigger: never - no write-back to any persistent store occurs.
failure_experience_usage: N/A - no success or failure experiences are stored or retrieved (no memory). Failures are only analyzed qualitatively in a case study, not fed back.
memory_evolution_update: N/A - no stored entries to mutate (no memory).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: false - the WHEN-to-retrieve decision is a fixed thresholded heuristic over a hand-designed score (entropy * max-attention * semantic indicator), and the WHAT (query) is a fixed top-attention token selection; neither the trigger policy nor the query/passage selection is an RL- or value-learned policy. The retrieval itself is fixed BM25/SGPT top-3.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A - single-model, single-agent inference; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing.
benchmarks: 2WikiMultihopQA, HotpotQA, StrategyQA, IIRC (top-1000 questions sampled per dataset). External corpus: Wikipedia (DPR psgs_w100, ~21M 100-token passages). LLMs evaluated: LLaMA-2-7B-Chat, LLaMA-2-13B-Chat, Vicuna-13B-v1.5.
benchmark_family: QA / multi-hop (2WikiMultihopQA, HotpotQA) plus reading comprehension (IIRC) and commonsense reasoning (StrategyQA) - all knowledge-intensive open-domain QA.
baselines: wo-RAG (no retrieval / direct answer); SR-RAG (single-round RAG, retrieve once from initial question); FL-RAG (fix-length RAG, retrieve every n tokens using last token window as query); FS-RAG (fix-sentence RAG, retrieve every sentence using last sentence as query); FLARE (retrieve when a token's probability is below threshold, query = last sentence minus low-probability tokens). Ablation comparisons also include 'Full Context' as query. All multi-round baselines re-implemented under FLARE's protocol so only the when/what differs.
key_metrics: Exact Match (EM), token-level F1, and token-level Precision for 2WikiMultihopQA / HotpotQA / IIRC; Accuracy for StrategyQA (yes/no exact match). Efficiency measured as the average number of retrieval-module activations (retrieval calls) per question.
headline_result: DRAGIN achieves the best results on most LLM x dataset cells across all four benchmarks. Most-cited example: on HotpotQA with LLaMA2-13B-Chat, DRAGIN reaches EM 0.314 / F1 0.4238, vs the best baseline FS-RAG 0.267 / 0.3715 and single-round SR-RAG 0.263 / 0.3706 (and wo-RAG 0.223 / 0.3097). On 2WikiMultihopQA (LLaMA2-13B-Chat) DRAGIN gets EM 0.304 / F1 0.3931 vs FS-RAG 0.270 / 0.3610. Gains are largest on multi-hop QA and smaller on StrategyQA commonsense reasoning.
ablations: (1) Timing-of-retrieval ablation (Table 4, IIRC): with query formulation fixed to the last sentence, RIND timing beats FLARE/FL-RAG/FS-RAG triggers (LLaMA2-13B EM 0.187 vs FS-RAG 0.171; Vicuna-13B EM 0.196 vs FS-RAG 0.103). (2) RIND threshold sensitivity (Table 5, HotpotQA, LLaMA2-13B): performance is stable across theta in [0.3,1.0] (EM 0.293-0.304, peak F1 ~0.394), and higher theta reduces retrieval frequency (efficiency-accuracy knob). (3) Query-formulation ablation (Table 6, HotpotQA): with timing fixed to RIND, QFS beats FLARE, FS-RAG, FL-RAG, and even Full-Context queries (LLaMA2-13B EM 0.314 vs FLARE 0.262, Full-Context 0.252), showing full context adds redundancy. (4) Retriever ablation (Table 7): BM25 consistently beats SGPT inside DRAGIN (e.g., HotpotQA LLaMA2-13B EM 0.314/F1 0.424 BM25 vs 0.264/0.371 SGPT). (5) Efficiency (Table 3): DRAGIN uses fewer retrieval calls than FS-RAG/FL-RAG (e.g., ~2.6-3.5 on multi-hop) though more than FLARE.
evaluation_decoupling: No - only end-to-end task metrics (EM/F1/Precision/Accuracy) are reported. No intrinsic retrieval-quality metric (Recall@k / nDCG / gold-passage recall) is reported separately; retrieval quality is only argued indirectly via downstream gains and a qualitative QFS-vs-FLARE query case study.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics (final-answer EM/F1/Precision/Accuracy). The only process-level signal is the retrieval-activation frequency (efficiency) and a qualitative case study of the generated query; no quantitative reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise retrieval-accuracy score.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported as average number of retrieval calls per question (Table 3): FLARE is the most efficient (fewest calls, e.g., ~0.6-1.6 on several sets but with weaker accuracy), DRAGIN is next (~2.5-4.8 depending on dataset/LLM), using fewer calls than FS-RAG (~3.1-6.8) and FL-RAG (~3.2-4.2). The RIND threshold theta directly trades retrieval frequency (cost/latency) against accuracy, and the threshold ablation shows accuracy is robust as theta increases (so cost can be cut with little accuracy loss). No dollar-cost or wall-clock latency table is reported. [uncertain] exact latency/dollar figures.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k injection: retrieve_topk = 3 passages per retrieval event, each ~100 tokens; on a new trigger these replace the prior 3 (not accumulated). Query token budget: top-n (retrieve_keep_top_k ~35-40) highest-attention content tokens. generate_max_length = 64; fewshot = 6 demonstrations. k is fixed (not adaptive/precision-driven); the variable quantity is the NUMBER of retrieval events, governed by the RIND threshold.
builds_on: FLARE (Jiang et al. 2023) - the closest active/dynamic RAG predecessor that triggers retrieval on low next-token probability and queries with the last sentence; fixed-schedule iterative RAG (FS-RAG following IRCoT/Trivedi et al. 2022; FL-RAG following kNN-LM Khandelwal et al. 2019, RETRO Borgeaud et al. 2022, In-Context RALM Ram et al. 2023); the retrieve-and-read RAG paradigm (Lewis et al. 2020, REALM/Guu et al. 2020, REPLUG/Shi et al. 2023); BM25 (Robertson et al.); SGPT (Muennighoff 2022); Transformer self-attention; chain-of-thought prompting (Wei et al. 2022). Base LLMs: LLaMA-2-Chat (Touvron et al. 2023b), Vicuna-13B-v1.5 (Chiang et al. 2023).
contrasts_with: FLARE (static next-token-probability trigger; query = last sentence minus low-prob tokens) - DRAGIN argues this trigger is suboptimal (good query strategy but poor timing) and that the query should span the whole context; fixed-rule multi-round RAG (FL-RAG per-n-tokens, FS-RAG per-sentence) which retrieve at fixed positions regardless of need; single-round SR-RAG (retrieve once from the question); no-retrieval wo-RAG; and using the Full Context as the query (shown to add redundancy).
lineage: Group B (retrieval-augmented task solving): a 2024 advance in the active/dynamic-RAG lineage of when-and-what-to-retrieve methods, directly succeeding FLARE and the IRCoT/FS-RAG line of CoT-guided iterative retrieval, and a frequently-reproduced predecessor to later step-wise/learned dynamic-RAG methods (e.g., DeepRAG, dynamic strategy planning, TC-RAG).
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A - not a case-based reasoning method (retrieves documents, not solved cases; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle).
explicit_cbr_grounding: false - the work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite CBR literature (Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner).
tool_document_engineering: N/A - no tools/skills are retrieved; only Wikipedia passages are indexed (raw 100-token text via BM25/SGPT, no description engineering).
index_content_separation: N/A - single flat passage index; no lightweight-index-then-content / progressive-disclosure separation.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A - no tool index or tool-integration protocol; static document corpus only.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A - no inter-tool dependency modeling (no tools).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A - not a CBR method; retrieved passages are used verbatim as in-context evidence, not adapted as cases.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A - this is a method paper, not a survey/taxonomy.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A - this is a method paper, not a benchmark paper; it reuses existing datasets (2WikiMultihopQA, HotpotQA, StrategyQA, IIRC), evaluating the top-1000 questions per dataset over a Wikipedia DPR corpus of ~21M 100-token passages.
